text: The road made Cnocby by a coin’s width, three chances of it against two of nothing, and the mountain timber that raised the travelers’ inn is mostly cut out. text: A free hamlet with no lord's representative. Communal elder consensus governs shared affairs.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: All family heads hold equal voice on shared concerns. Slower but more egalitarian.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A steward appointed by a distant lord to oversee the settlement. Authority is formal but often resented.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: One household head acts as de facto voice for the settlement. No formal appointment, no title. Just the person everyone goes to when something needs deciding.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A lord's steward collects rents and enforces manor authority over a bound village.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A single respected figure acts as de facto authority. Not elected, not appointed, simply acknowledged. Decisions are practical rather than formal.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Elected from the peasantry. Organises labour obligations, mediates disputes, and represents the village to outside authority.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The oldest or most respected resident guides village decisions in the absence of formal authority. Less official than a reeve, more stable than nothing.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Elected civic council with full administrative apparatus.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Guilds control town politics. The guildmasters sit on the council.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A lord's appointed official governs; noble authority supersedes local custom.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: An informal council of prominent citizens manages town affairs in the absence of formal authority. Less accountable than an elected council, more stable than nothing.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A consortium of guild masters holds effective civic power.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A royal or ducal appointee governs; the city operates as a noble fief.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Wealthy merchant families hold exclusive civic power; political office is effectively purchased.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The settlement governs itself and its surrounding territory as an independent polity. No higher lord, no external charter.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A citizen assembly holds formal authority; eligible voters debate and vote on major ordinances and appointments.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A royal governor or viceroy administers directly on behalf of the crown. High status, high scrutiny.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: An administrative apparatus of officials, clerks, and ward officers manages city affairs. Less formally constituted than a council but functional. Governance by bureaucratic inertia.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Seat of metropolitan or state government: palace, ministries, audience halls, administrative bureaux.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Specialized courts (commercial, criminal, appellate, ecclesiastical) operating simultaneously.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Simple prayer location. No clergy.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Travel to village church. 2-5km distance typical.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A walled plot at the edge of the settlement, gated against livestock and kept by the households in turn. The rite is held when a priest comes through, and the burial itself does not wait for one. Families lie in rows by household rather than by standing, which is custom here rather than poverty.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Center of village life. Stone construction. Mandatory tithes.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A resident singer, fiddler, or piper. Plays at festivals and weddings. Also a keeper of local history through song.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Performs sacraments, collects tithes. Often only literate person.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Consecrated ground beside the church, on the parish's own plot, with a resident priest to close it. The rite keeps to the day of the death rather than waiting on a clergyman who comes through, and the parish has begun keeping the names in the same book as the baptisms. The ground nearest the church wall is spoken for generations ahead, and everyone here can say who holds it.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple parishes within town.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Religious community. May operate hospital/school.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Care for sick poor. Usually religious-run.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Each parish keeps its own ground beside its church, and a parish that has filled its ground buries beyond the gate instead. The sexton holds the register of who lies where, which is the town's longest unbroken record and the one it reaches for in an inheritance dispute. Guilds buy plots together so their members lie among their trade.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Bishop's seat. Requires 10,000+ population minimum. Defines major city status.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Large facility for sick poor. 50-100 beds.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Receives abandoned infants and young children, providing basic care until they can be apprenticed, placed with families, or raised within the institution. Usually church-run. The wheel in the wall allows anonymous deposit at night.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The parish grounds inside the walls filled generations ago, so the dead are lifted once their term is up and their bones stacked in the charnel house to make room for the next. New ground has been bought outside the gates, and the carts that go out at dusk are a fixed part of the city's evening. Who is lifted and who is left where they lie is settled by what a family endowed.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Hundreds of parish churches across all districts. The faith is woven into every neighbourhood.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Metropolitan cathedral. Seat of the highest regional religious authority. Pilgrimage destination.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Five to ten major monastic houses: scholarly, contemplative, and charitable functions at scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple hospitals and infirmaries across districts. Organized medical care at population scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Burial has left the walls entirely: grounds beyond every gate, each with its own road, its own gatekeepers, and a trade in plots that the revenue office watches. The parish registers are copied into a central roll because no parish can any longer say where its own dead are. Wards are assigned to grounds, so a family that moves across the city can find itself divided by the assignment.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Somebody in this settlement buys things without asking where they came from. Everyone knows who. Nobody says it directly.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Someone here provides cover for people who need to disappear. A barn, a cellar, an arrangement that isn't discussed.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Local contact for moving stolen goods quietly. Operates behind another trade.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: One or more households here have ties to bandit groups operating the surrounding roads. Information, shelter, and supply flow both ways.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Goods pass through here to avoid toll roads or customs checkpoints. The hamlet benefits from fees paid in kind.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: An extensive warren of smuggling tunnels beneath the city.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organized pickpockets and thugs. 10-30 members.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Illicit goods trade. Tax evasion.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Warehouses, taverns, shops as criminal covers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A loft of message birds kept by people who file no returns. Word arrives unsigned and ahead of the watch. Only a standing criminal organization can protect a loft like this, so one never appears without that backing.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organized crime chapter. 10,000+ population for viable operation. 30-100 members.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Competing gangs. Turf disputes.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Illicit goods trade. Hidden locations.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: An individual or small cell operating beneath the assassins guild threshold. Accepts contracts through criminal intermediaries. Less reliable but deniable.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Targets free persons for fraudulent insertion into slavery through forged provenance documents. Where no lawful market exists to absorb the traffic, it runs its own holding, its own escorts, and its own silence.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Fully clandestine operation moving persons across jurisdictions outside legal channels. Only fires where no legal slave market exists. Distinct logistics, safe houses, and corrupt border infrastructure.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The covert guild form: brokers who buy and sell knowledge by the piece, grade what they sell, and will manufacture a claim for a patron who pays enough. It sites itself where the talk already is, among the fences, the late houses, and the inns that ask nothing.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Dominant criminal syndicate. Tolerated because the alternative (gang war) is worse.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Permanent underground market: contraband, forged documents, illegal services.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Extensive tunnels and catacombs repurposed as criminal and refugee sanctuary.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Professional contract killing. Operates through cutouts, never acknowledged officially.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Wattle-and-daub or timber. 1-2 rooms per household.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Well or spring access.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Sharpened stakes encircling the settlement. Offers minimal protection but enough to deter casual raiders.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: One able-bodied adult from each household musters with hunting bows, spears, and farm tools when danger reaches the fields.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A shared underground store for grain, roots, and preserved food. Vital buffer against a bad harvest.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Timber-frame with thatched roofs.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Wells, fountains, or piped water.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Timber construction with stone foundations.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Meeting place and administrative center.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Borough court for local justice.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Holding cells and public punishment.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multi-story timber and stone buildings.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Commercial, criminal, and ecclesiastical courts.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Debtors, criminals, political prisoners.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The able-bodied poor receive shelter and food in exchange for compulsory labour: textile work, grinding, construction. Not a prison but the line is blurry. Reduces vagrancy and produces goods. Conditions are deliberately harsh to discourage dependency.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Underground drainage. Rare but critical for health.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multi-story buildings. Tenements for poor.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Engineered water supply. Conduits, cisterns, fountains.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: State prison complex: political prisoners, debtors, convicted criminals held separately.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple aqueducts, cisterns, and distributed fountains. City-wide water management at scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Manor mill with milling monopoly (banalité).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Strip farming in open fields.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Nets, traps, and drying racks. The settlement's economy is inseparable from the water.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Communal flock management. The rhythms of the settlement follow the grazing calendar.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Seasonal felling and timber stacking. The whole settlement smells of fresh sawdust and pine resin.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Home-brewed ale sold from someone's back room. The hamlet's main gathering place. News, disputes, and arrangements all happen here.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A room above a stable and a common meal for travelers passing through. Exists because the road does.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A substantial walled compound for desert merchants: stabling for camels, locked storage, a well, and sleeping quarters for fifty. The economic hub of any desert settlement that sees caravan traffic.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Monthly or seasonal trading day. No charter. Just habit, proximity, and a flat piece of ground.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Lending against pledged goods. High interest, no questions. The only credit available to peasants and small craftsmen.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Shared pasture for village livestock.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Open-field agriculture with crop rotation.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A single inn serving traders, pilgrims, and travelers passing through. Rooms, stabling, and a common meal.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Royal charter required. Major economic driver.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Home-based. Women brew and sell ale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A flat-bottomed ferry crossing the river. The ferryman's family has held the crossing rights for generations. Essential for anyone who doesn't want a long walk to the nearest bridge.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Builds and repairs flat-bottomed river craft: barges, punts, ferries, fishing boats. Specialist knowledge of river construction: shallow draft, flexible hull, replaceable parts.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: An open-air stall or small covered market where the day's catch is sold. Prices drop fast. Fish doesn't wait.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A bridge with a toll house. The keeper collects passage fees and performs basic maintenance. Minor but steady revenue.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A fortified overnight stop with stabling, a well, and basic provisions. Serves merchant caravans and long-distance travellers. Distinct from the inn. Built for animals and loaded wagons, not comfort.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Communal grain storage. Buffers harvests, prevents famine.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Central plaza for weekly markets and fairs. 50-100 yards per side.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Regional merchants. Luxury goods available.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Control trade in specific goods.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Regulate quality, prices, and apprenticeships.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Exchange foreign currency. Early banking (3,000+ population).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Lodging for traveling merchants.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Drinking establishments. Social hubs.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: If coastal or river access. Essential for bulk trade.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A guild of professional carters, teamsters, and pack-animal drivers who move goods overland for hire. They know every road, every toll, every seasonal closure, and they charge accordingly.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Purpose-built for road travellers: stabling for relay horses, scheduled coach departures, meals served at fixed hours, and a passenger waiting room. Horses changed here, not just rested.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Communal bathing facility with heated water. In some cultures a social hub; in others suspect as a venue for vice. Either way, the best place in the town to hear rumour and news.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A yard where carters, teamsters, and pack-animal drivers can be hired for the road. Returning drivers share road conditions and bandit reports over a cup of ale. Transactional, not institutional.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: City-scale shipyard constructing large merchant and war vessels. Multiple dry docks, ropewalk, sail loft, and dedicated ironworks. A major employer and a strategic military asset.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Established auction block with holding facilities, registered brokers, and provenance documentation. Legally sanctioned commerce in persons: taxed, regulated, and embedded in the city economy.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Sells road maps, regional surveys, and coastal charts. Takes commissions for estate surveys and dungeon sketching. Maintains a reference collection of older maps for consultation. Standard stop for adventurers, merchants, and military scouts.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Tests the purity of precious metals brought to the town. Essential infrastructure for banking and minting. Charges fees per assay.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Levies duties on goods entering and leaving via the port or main roads. Run by royal or municipal officials.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Maintains a team of horses for rapid message relay. Letters and small packages travel far faster than foot traffic. Requires coaching inn.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Concentrated stabling, horse trading, and farriery. Serves merchants, military, and travelers needing fresh mounts.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Coordinates regional caravan assembly, departure schedules, and route intelligence. Merchants register goods, hire guards, and arrange joint ventures here. The town-scale predecessor to the city's Caravan masters' exchange.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Works precious metals and gemstones into rings, necklaces, seals, and luxury items. Accepts commissions, appraises stones, and occasionally buys stolen goods from discreet customers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Produces and ages wine, either from local grapes or imported must. Sells in bulk to taverns and directly to wealthy clients. A vintner in a non-wine region is an importer-blender.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A licensed house that pays for road news and keeps the register: who arrived, from where, and what they carried word of. Cheap to run and openly taxed, which is why it appears wherever traffic does and nowhere that it does not.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple large grain stores distribute food across the city. State managed.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple permanent market squares serve different districts.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Superseded at metropolis scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple inn districts catering to merchants, travelers, and long-term visitors.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: International merchants. Letters of credit accepted.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Loans, currency exchange, letters of credit. Basic banking (5,000+).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Extreme specialization (gold-beaters, mirror-makers).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Storage for merchant goods.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Operates a fleet of river barges on scheduled and commissioned runs. Carries bulk cargo, passengers, and military supply along the river network.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The city-scale version: permanent offices where caravan masters, merchants, and armed escorts transact. Bonded freight, route intelligence, armed convoy assembly, and commercial dispute resolution.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A permanent, licensed district for commerce in persons: auction halls, holding compounds, broker offices, and associated legal and financial infrastructure. Operates at a scale beyond a single market block.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A guild of professional cartographers producing regional maps, sea charts, property surveys, and military reconnaissance maps. Sells off-the-shelf maps and takes commissions. The city's maps are the most accurate in the region.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple apothecary shops clustered together. Competition drives specialization. Some focus on chirurgery, others on herbal preparations, others on imported medicines. Herbalism kits, medicinal herbs, surgical supplies, and basic antidotes all available.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: State or noble-chartered coin production. Standardises currency across the region. Significant ongoing revenue via seigniorage.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Formal venue for selling high-value goods: estates, ships, livestock, art, and occasionally persons. Charges buyer's and seller's premiums.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Regulates harbour and river-port traffic, collects anchorage fees, assigns berths, and enforces port law. Navigable-water cities only.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Fur processors, traders, and retailers concentrated in one area. High-value trade. Quality furs are luxury goods.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: The guild form of the listening house: paid correspondents on several roads, an archive that cross-checks one road against another, and a standing rate for a written answer. Expensive to keep, and the only counter in the city where a claim is graded before it is sold.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Five to ten permanent specialized market districts: grain, livestock, cloth, metals, exotica.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Dozens of merchant guilds representing every major trade good and route. A formal guild parliament.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Consolidated financial quarter: international banking, letters of credit, currency speculation at scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Hub for international merchant representatives, trade arbitration, and commodity exchange.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: State-administered granary network holding strategic reserves.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Repairs tools, shoes horses. Farms also.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Builds/repairs buildings and tools.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A rough landing with racks for drying and salting fish. Primary protein source near water.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organises hunting parties across the surrounding territory. Sells venison, pelts, and game to market. Doubles as a source of local wilderness knowledge: which trails are safe, which aren't.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Operates kilns in the surrounding woodland, supplying fuel for smithing, baking, and heating. The settlement's most reliable fuel source when timber is abundant.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Converts barley into malt for brewing. Small operation supplying local alehouses. Requires grain surplus.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Cuts and dries peat blocks from nearby marshland for domestic fuel. Seasonal. Sells winter warmth.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Communal stable where travelers can leave horses. Stableman provides basic farriery and fodder.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A shallow excavation or shaft dug to extract iron ore, coal, or stone. Employs the poorest labourers. Dangerous, dirty, and essential.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Systematic extraction of building stone. A village on good quarry land can supply half a region's construction needs, and the quarry master knows it.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Buys and sells mules, donkeys, and draft horses. Rents animals to travellers and merchants who need load-carrying capacity for the road.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Keeps cattle or goats for milk, butter, and soft cheese. Essential protein and fat during lean grain seasons. Sells surplus at the weekly market.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Manages sheep flocks for wool and meat. Seasonal transhumance. Moves flocks between lowland winter pasture and upland summer grazing. Key supplier to the textile trade.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Evaporation pans or brine processing along the coast or riverbank. Salt is the settlement's most traded commodity by weight. Every household needs it.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Water or windmill with monopoly milling rights. The miller is often the wealthiest and most resented figure in the village.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Full-time metalworker. Essential for tools and horseshoes.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Builds houses, carts, furniture.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Roof repair and construction.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Makes barrels for storage and transport.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Sells herbal medicines, poultices, and common remedies. Distinct from the alchemist. No magical compounds, no acid flasks. Knows which roots treat fever and which mushrooms kill. Stocked with herbalism supplies.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Makes bows, crossbows, and arrows. Sells finished ammunition and takes custom bow commissions. The first stop for any adventurer whose quiver is empty.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Water- or ox-powered saw. Converts raw logs to planks and beams. Expands construction and furniture output.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A shaft or excavation to extract iron ore, coal, or stone. Requires capital and organisation a thorp cannot sustain, but a village near deposits can. Employs the poorest labourers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Converts hides into leather using oak bark. Foul-smelling. Placed downstream. Essential for shoes, harness, and straps.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Finishes woven cloth by cleaning and thickening it. Often water-powered. Transforms raw weave into durable textile.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Applies colour to raw or woven cloth. Essential for producing anything beyond undyed grey wool.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Wheel-thrown pottery for domestic use. Plates, jugs, storage vessels. Fired in a small kiln.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Moulds and fires clay bricks for construction. Enables more permanent buildings. Requires clay deposits and fuel.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Converts malted grain to ale in quantity. The largest consumer of grain after bread. Supplies alehouses and households.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Maintains stabling, trains horses for riding and draft work. Essential for any settlement on a road.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Maintains hives for honey and beeswax. Honey sweetens; beeswax makes candles, wax seals, and polish.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Buys, salts, and sells fish. The link between fishing and consumption. Near water: fresh. Inland: dried or salted.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Makes and repairs shoes and boots. Every person needs footwear. One of the most reliable and consistent trades.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Cuts and sews finished cloth into garments. Serves the middle tier between home seamstress and master clothier.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Assists with births, manages difficult labours, and provides basic gynecological care. The most-used medical service in any settlement.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Can read and write. Copies letters, draws up simple contracts, reads documents for the illiterate. Often the priest's assistant or a monastery-educated lay person.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Catches waterfowl and game birds using nets, traps, and trained birds. Supplies the market with ducks, geese, and pigeons.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Carves functional and decorative items from wood: tool handles, religious figures, furniture inlays. Produces sacred images and reliquaries for the church.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A craftsman who draws and sells maps: regional road maps, property surveys, and rough wilderness sketches from traveler accounts. Rare enough that most villages don't have one.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple mills for grain, fulling cloth.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple smiths with specializations.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Construction and furniture makers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Cloth production. Often guild-organized.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Leather production. Foul-smelling; sited by water and toward the settlement edge where the ground allows.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Meat processing. Strictly regulated.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Bread production. Guild-regulated prices.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A proper shop with a trained herbalist, stocked inventory, and a back room for consultations. Sells herbalism kit supplies, common antidotes, medicinal herbs, and basic surgical dressings. Some double as chirurgeons.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple craftsmen organized under a guild. Standard arrows by the sheaf, specialty broadheads, composite bows to commission. Restocks merchant caravans and outfits town militias.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Converts raw ore to refined metal using charcoal-fueled furnaces. The industrial intermediate between mine and smithy.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A water- or ox-powered mill producing planks and beams for the construction trade. A town near timber can supply an entire region's building needs. Employs a permanent crew.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Commercial-scale ale and beer production. Supplies the town's taverns and regional distribution. Major grain consumer and employer.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Full-scale tannery with multiple vats and a guild-trained workforce. Produces high-quality leather for shoes, armour, and saddlery.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organised shoemakers producing boots, shoes, and sandals for the urban population. Strictly regulated quality.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Master clothiers producing garments from finished cloth. Produces everything from working clothes to livery.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Makes candles from tallow and beeswax. Also produces soap and rope from similar raw materials. Essential for lighting.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Small-scale glasswork: bottles, window panes, goblets. Requires silica sand, potash, and a skilled furnace operator.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Converts refined precious metal into standardised coinage. Requires noble or royal charter. Significant revenue for the granting authority.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Official announcer who reads proclamations, market prices, and news at fixed times in the market square. Employed by the town or a guild.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Twists fibres (hemp, flax, or plant matter) into rope and cordage. Essential for ships, construction, and agriculture.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Armorers, swordsmiths, jewelers. Separate guilds.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Silks, spices, precious goods.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Books and broadsheets (if technology exists).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Windows, vessels, mirrors. Requires expertise.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Over a hundred distinct craft specializations. A guild for every conceivable trade.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Occasional visits. The smallest spells only.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A licensed charter hall providing bounties, monster-hunting coordination, and emergency armed response for the surrounding territory. More common in frontier regions.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A resident caster of modest reach. Minor spells only.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A circle of druids tied to the land. They regulate the seasons, mediate disputes with wild creatures, and know which streams run clean. More common in forested or isolated settlements, but they adapt. Some circles tend city gardens or hidden urban groves.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Basic healing spells. A closed wound costs 10 in gold.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: High-level spellcaster residence. Multiple towers possible.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A council of senior druids who govern their circle's relationship with the city. They may maintain a hidden grove beneath the streets, mediate between urban expansion and wild places, or serve as ecological advisors to the ruling authority. Found in cities that have made peace with nature magic.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Potions, alchemical items. Basic healing potions (50 in gold).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A ranger station or druid waypost. They monitor the surrounding wilderness, maintain trails, and keep tabs on beast migrations. In times of crisis they serve as emergency scouts and trackers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Permanent teleportation circle. Access is controlled and expensive to maintain. Transformative infrastructure for any settlement lucky enough to have one.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organization of magic users. 2,000-5,000 population for chapter.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple alchemical workshops. Guild organization.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Magic item creation. 5,000+ population typically.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Spell scrolls for sale. 25 in gold for the smallest charm, 500 and up for a greater working.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Formal institution of arcane learning. Full curriculum, research facilities, visiting scholars.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Quarter inhabited by arcane practitioners: towers, workshops, libraries, reagent merchants.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Largest repository of knowledge in the region: thousands of volumes, map archives, historical records.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Formal diplomatic mission from a planar power. Trade, information, occasional intervention.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: All able-bodied citizens obligated to defend town. Part-time service. Present only when no professional watch exists.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Perimeter palisade or earthwork berm. Controls approach, slows attackers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A drinking hall where retired soldiers and mercenaries gather. Informal security, bar brawls, and the occasional job offer for a group needing swords.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Stone fortifications with gates. Expensive to build and maintain.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Part-time guards. Night patrol and gate duty.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Controlled entry points with gatekeepers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Housing for guards or small garrison.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A billet and contracting office for a band of professional soldiers available between campaigns. Offers caravan escort, garrison contracts, and short-term military hire at day-wage rates. Cheaper than a standing army, more reliable than a mob. These men fight in formation on salary, not for treasure.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Masonry walls with towers. Multiple gatehouses.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Full-time law enforcement. ~1% of population.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Professional soldiers. Noble or royal.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Inner fortress. Last refuge in siege.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Layered wall systems: outer wall, inner wall, citadel ring. Multiple garrison zones and gatehouses.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Garrison forces distributed across quarters. No single barracks can secure a metropolis.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Warehouse facilities for merchants storing goods awaiting sale, transit, or seasonal distribution. Essential infrastructure for any trade route settlement.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Job board for torchbearers (1 in gold a session), porters (5 in gold a session).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: A chartered hall serving as the primary adventuring hub for the region. Posts contracts, grades monster threats, maintains gear, and coordinates large-scale operations that militia cannot handle.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Non-magical 'divination' using Deception. 1-5 in gold.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Common animals only. Horses, dogs, falcons.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Organized sellsword companies. Major forces (hundreds to thousands).
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Specialized adventuring gear. Warded weapons, silver weapons, etc.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Multiple scholars and researchers.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Bards, jugglers, acrobats visit during fairs.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Dice, cards, simple games of chance.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Trains fighters for public spectacle. Recruits from prisoners, debtors, and volunteers. Feeds the arena circuit.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Individual or small groups of professional fighters available for private contracts: bodyguard work, debt enforcement, or quiet removal of problems.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Tolerated or regulated prostitution.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Dedicated establishments. Some illegal.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Legal or tolerated prostitution quarter.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Illegal or semi-legal combat. Underground locations.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Permanent venues. Professional companies.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Gladiatorial games or monster fights. Massive scale.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Large organized prostitution quarter.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Concentrated gaming houses. Play kept honest by compelled truth.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: High culture. Elite patronage.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Formal musical education. Amphitheater, dormitories. 10,000+ for small campus.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Goods from other planes of existence.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Ancient wyrm living in city.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Constructed servants if magic permits.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Animated corpses working. Controversial.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Dream-walking magic sold as experience. Lucid shared dreams, communication.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Mooring towers with magical weather protection.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271

text: Paired Speaking Stones set in a network. 250-10,000 in gold per station.
note: truncateAtWord(instDef.desc,80) on the institution card; full text at :271
